messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] Customer: Velvet Analytics (dedicated pool eu-west-2) — p99 latency crossing SLO (500ms) for the last 6m. Impact: interactive queries degraded. Paging oncall.
jamie-oncall: I’m on it. Paging execs and AM. Starting triage.
rosa-AM: I'm on standby. Notifying Velvet account team. Sam, are you seeing errors on your side? :phone_receiver:
sam.velvet: We see UI timeouts for some dashboards ~2m ago. Nothing changed on our side. Can't access some historical queries.
lee-runtime: Checking pool telemetry now. Real-time dashboard shows spike coincident with a request pattern change — tail latencies up. No node failures yet.
anya-ml: Do we have any model rollouts or quantization changes for that pool? I didn't see any recent model swaps for Velvet's pinned model.
kyle-infra: No infra deploys in eu-west-2. Networking appears normal. Host CPU is fine but GPU utilization spiked on a subset of nodes.
lucas-support: Logging customer impact: velvet internal docs mention 250+ active users — flagging severity high.
jamie-oncall: Hypothesis: a tenant-specific traffic burst causing KV-cache churn. Steps: 1) isolate tenant to limited capacity 2) enable per-tenant throttle 3) scale dedicated pool if needed. Any objections?
lee-runtime: Agreed. I can apply a temporary per-tenant throttle and enable prefix KV caching for the tenant to reduce recompute pressure.
ops-bot: Runbook invoked: "dedicated-pool-tenant-isolation". Playbook owner: jamie-oncall. Notifying SRE rotation.
jamie-oncall: lucas, can you DM Sam the mitigation plan and ask for any nonstandard query workloads started? rosa, please keep Velvet PM updated.
rosa-AM: On it. Sam, please share any recent report exports or scheduled jobs that could explain burst.
sam.velvet: We did kick off a cohort backfill job this morning but it should be hitting a different workspace. I'll confirm. Sending logs.
lee-runtime: Applying throttle: ```rtsctl tenant throttle --tenant velvet-123 --qps 10 --reason "temp SLO containment"``` Applying now.
ops-bot: Command accepted. Throttle applied to tenant velvet-123 (qps 10). Monitoring effect.
anya-ml: While we throttle, we should try switching Velvet to the lighter model variant (quantized) if acceptable. Lower throughput per-request latency.
rosa-AM: Sam, can Velvet accept a temporary model fallback for 15–30m? It may change output fidelity slightly.
sam.velvet: We can accept temporary fallback for dashboards only. Backfill must finish unchanged; we'll keep jobs on hold if needed.
kyle-infra: I’m spinning up +2 nodes in their dedicated pool (type gtx-4x) as a burst capacity. ETA ~2m.
lee-runtime: Noted. After throttle, p99 dropped from ~1.6s to ~780ms in first check. Still above 500ms but trending down.
jamie-oncall: Good. Continue monitoring. If p99 > SLO after scale, we escalate to forced tenant eviction (last resort) and route traffic to hosted fallback.
lucas-support: Documenting timeline and customer comms in casebook. Will prepare status message for Velvet users.
ops-bot: Autoscale event: +2 nodes added to velvet-123 pool (node IDs: node-ev-22, node-ev-23). Capacity online.
lee-runtime: After nodes came up, p99 is ~430ms. Throughput stable. KV hit rate improved after throttle and extra nodes.
anya-ml: Can we run a lightweight eval on the fallback quantized variant to validate dashboard regressions? I can run 50 sample queries.
rosa-AM: Do that, Anya. Sam, we’ll only flip dashboards to quantized variant pending your OK — metrics-first approach.
sam.velvet: OK to flip dashboards after eval. Please keep backfill untouched.
jamie-oncall: Moving to containment->mitigation. Next: 1) keep throttle 2) keep extra nodes for 15m 3) run eval 4) coordinate with customer for rollback window. I'll schedule a 20m check-in. :white_check_mark:
lucas-support: Sending Velvet status: "We've applied temporary throttles and added capacity; dashboards may be routed to a lower-latency model variant temporarily. We'll update within 20 minutes." 
sam.velvet: Received. Thank you for the quick response.
lee-runtime: Adding a trace sample for one high-latency request and posting stacktrace to thread: ```trace_id: t-9a7f, model: rtx-3b-v1, kv_miss: true, note: heavy prefix churn observed```
kyle-infra: No disk/network alarms. GPU memory pressure on node-ev-21 peaked; newer nodes offload some load.
jamie-oncall: Handoff plan: jamie -> next-oncall (in 25m) if p99 < SLO and stable. Otherwise keep paged. I'll leave this thread open and annotate final timeline.
ops-bot: Incident status: Contained -> Mitigated? (monitoring). Record ID: INC-2026-5556.
jamie-oncall: Final note for incident log: root cause likely tenant workload spike (backfill + dashboard queries) causing KV-cache churn on dedicated pool; mitigations: per-tenant throttle, temporary scale, optional model fallback. Follow-ups: autoscale tuning, per-tenant guardrails, doc for customers on backfill best practices.
rosa-AM: I'll schedule a postmortem with Velvet this week and coordinate an engineering changelist.
sam.velvet: Please include our runbook triggers so we can avoid surprise throttles next time. Appreciate the quick mitigation.
lee-runtime: Closing loop: p99 stable at 420ms for last 5m. Will remove temporary throttle after 30m if stable and notify customer.
jamie-oncall: Thanks team. Closing active paging. :tada:
